unit.why: A first-person memorate of a Sabbath visit to the Seer of Lublin, in which cups of wine the narrator refuses to drink keep cracking on the table.

stories.start_quote: המעשה הב׳ אח״כ כשהייתי מעט לאיש
stories.summary_en: As a young man the narrator spends Shabbat with R. Jacob Isaac of Lublin and keeps his custom of not drinking intoxicants; the wine cups the Seer sets before him crack one after another until the narrator explains himself and the Seer stops offering.

quotes: נסעתי להרב הצדיק הקדוש מוה׳ ר׳ יעקב יצחק
tags.why: The narrator travels to the Seer of Lublin for Shabbat.

quotes: ובליל ש״ק נת נתן לידי צלוחית יין
tags.why: The scene takes place on Friday night at the Sabbath table.
The plot turns on the wine offered at the table and the narrator's refusal to drink it.

quotes: שמנהגי היה שלא לשתות שום משקה המשכר
tags.why: The narrator keeps a personal custom of abstaining from intoxicating drink.

quotes: ועמד כ״כ הרבה עד שנתבקע ונשפך היין
tags.why: The cups crack on their own, which reads as a wondrous event.

quotes: ולסרב בדברי הרב ג״כ לא נכון
tags.why: The narrator effectively declines the tzaddik's instruction to drink.
The tension between deference to the rebbe and the young visitor's own custom is the heart of the story.

quotes: הנה באת לשבר כל הזכוכית שלי
tags.why: The Seer's remark about the broken glasses sounds like a wry jest.
The tzaddik hosts a young visitor at his table.

missing_concepts: personal religious custom (minhag) upheld against a tzaddik's wish
